title: Rogers City, Michigan: the Carl D. Bradley, November 18, 1958
notes: Viewer request (YouTube comment, Nov. 16, 2026). A real disaster: history only, no one shown in the water, no bodies. Numbers with disagreements left out or rounded: widows (23 or 25), children (53 or 54: 'more than 50'), Rogers City dead (23 in most sources; one says 26), how fast she sank, time on the raft (14 to 16 hours), depth. The two men lost from the raft and their names are left out. No cause given (Marine Board and Commandant disagreed). Blind check Nov. 21: '33 lost, 23 from Rogers City' (locals say 33); 'bound for Calcite, at Rogers City' (she had been headed for winter layup and was sent back for one more load); 'ABOUT 5:30 P.M.' (some say 5:35); no lightning (a gale, not a thunderstorm); a night departure; the memorial lists both the Bradley and Cedarville crews, and its anchor and propeller are not the Bradley's (Alpena News, 2017), so the drawing is just an anchor and the text never calls it hers.

beats.text: You asked for Rogers City, Michigan. In one night, 33 men were lost. 23 of them were from this small town.
beats.label: ROGERS CITY, MICHIGAN
beats.credit: History: Rogers City Sailors Memorial; WCMU; Presque Isle County Advance

beats.text: November 1958. The Bradley, a limestone freighter more than 600 feet long, left Gary, Indiana, empty, bound for Calcite, at Rogers City.
beats.label: LEFT GARY, NOVEMBER 17, 1958
beats.credit: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board report, 1959; NOAA; Wisconsin Marine Historical Society

beats.text: On Lake Michigan the next day, winds topped 60 miles an hour. Waves were about 25 feet high.
beats.label: NOVEMBER 18, 1958
beats.credit: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board report, 1959; WCMU; Wisconsin Marine Historical Society

beats.text: Around 5:30 that evening, the Bradley broke in two.
beats.label: ABOUT 5:30 P.M.
beats.credit: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board report, 1959; Wisconsin Marine Historical Society

beats.text: A Mayday went out, just as the power failed. Of 35 men aboard, 2 survived, on a raft, through the night.
beats.label: MAYDAY
beats.credit: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board report, 1959; Rogers City Sailors Memorial

beats.text: In Rogers City, more than 50 children lost their fathers.
beats.label: ROGERS CITY
beats.credit: Rogers City Sailors Memorial; WCMU; The Alpena News

beats.text: Today, a sailors' memorial by the lake in Rogers City lists the crew's names.
beats.label: ROGERS CITY SAILORS MEMORIAL
beats.credit: Rogers City Sailors Memorial marker; WCMU
